# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination — Request for Reconsideration

**Date:** [Date this letter is sent]

**To:** Molina Healthcare — Member Appeals
[Appeal address printed on my denial letter]

**From:** Riley Novak
[My mailing address]
[My phone number]

---

**RE: Appeal of denial dated 2026-08-10 — Reference number POC-1EC0B0CD1F-92337**
**Member:** Riley Novak
**Member ID:** W755986580
**Plan:** Molina Healthcare (Commercial/ACA), State of Mississippi
**Service denied:** Total shoulder replacement, CPT 23472
**Requesting surgeon:** Okafor, MD, orthopedic surgery

---

Dear Molina Healthcare Appeals Reviewer,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization for a total shoulder replacement (CPT 23472), which Molina Healthcare denied on 2026-08-10 under reference number POC-1EC0B0CD1F-92337. I am asking Molina to reconsider that decision and approve the surgery my surgeon has documented that I need.

## The specific criteria Molina applied have not been shared with me

The denial notice states that the determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria, and gives as the reason that the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure. However, the notice does not identify which policy or guideline was used, and no criteria language has been quoted to me. Because of that, I am not quoting any plan criteria in this letter — I will not put words in Molina's mouth, and I am not able to point to a specific imaging threshold the plan says I failed to meet, because none has been stated to me in writing.

**I am therefore requesting, in writing, the criteria Molina applied to my case.** Molina's utilization management information states that its criteria are MCG guidelines available through the secure provider portal, and that a member may call to obtain the criteria used to make a final determination. Please send me **the MCG guideline title and the specific criteria applied to my determination**, including the particular imaging findings the guideline requires, so that I and my surgeon can respond to them directly. If the surgery remains denied after this appeal, I ask that the denial letter identify the exact criterion I did not meet and the exact finding in my records that Molina believes falls short.

## What my medical records actually document

Until those criteria are provided, I can only present what is in my chart. My records document the following, and I am asking that each item be considered against whatever imaging standard Molina applied:

**Imaging (2026-06-05).** Shoulder radiographs, true AP and axillary views, show complete loss of the glenohumeral joint space, with osteophytes, subchondral sclerosis, and a flattened glenoid. A CT confirms an intact rotator cuff. These are objective, structural findings on standard views — not a subjective report of pain. Complete loss of joint space is the end point of joint space narrowing; there is no further degree of narrowing that could be demonstrated. The intact rotator cuff confirmed on CT is directly relevant to the choice of an anatomic total shoulder replacement.

**Duration of symptoms.** 24 months of progressive shoulder pain, unrelieved by rest.

**Conservative treatment, completed and documented.**
- Supervised physical therapy focused on range of motion and periscapular strengthening: 12 weeks, from 2026-04-27 to 2026-07-20, 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.
- NSAIDs for 6 months, with inadequate relief.
- Corticosteroid injection on 2026-06-17, which gave only 2 weeks of partial relief.

**Examination findings.** Glenohumeral crepitus; active forward elevation limited to 90 degrees; external rotation limited to 10 degrees; rotator cuff strength intact.

**Functional loss.** I cannot reach overhead, I cannot dress without help, and I cannot sleep on the affected side.

**Surgical risk factors.** No active infection, no untreated substance use, BMI 29, non-smoker.

My surgeon, Okafor, MD, has documented that this procedure is needed. The imaging, the examination findings, and the record of failed conservative care were all part of the prior authorization packet.

## What I am asking for

I respectfully request that Molina Healthcare:

1. Overturn the denial dated 2026-08-10 and approve CPT 23472 as medically necessary;
2. Provide me in writing the MCG guideline title and the specific criteria applied to my determination, including the imaging findings required; and
3. Have this appeal reviewed by a physician with training in orthopedic surgery.

I understand my appeal must be received by **2027-02-06**, within 180 days of the date of the denial notice, and I am submitting it within that window. I am sending this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, which is the authoritative address for my plan. I understand I may also use the Molina member portal at molinahealthcare.com or call the Member Services number on my ID card, and I will confirm the appeal window and address on my denial letter.

Please contact me at the phone number above if any additional records would help. My surgeon's office can also supply the complete imaging studies, operative planning notes, and physical therapy records on request.

Thank you for taking a second look at this decision.

Sincerely,

**Riley Novak**
Member ID: W755986580
Reference number: POC-1EC0B0CD1F-92337

[Signature]
[Date]

**Enclosures:** [List what you send — e.g., copy of denial notice dated 2026-08-10; radiograph and CT reports dated 2026-06-05; physical therapy discharge note covering 2026-04-27 to 2026-07-20; injection record dated 2026-06-17; surgeon's office notes]
